question: Despite having his leg blown off in a war, what is Mr. Lamb's general attitude towards life and other people? 🌻
options: He is bitter, angry, and hides in his house 😠
He is highly optimistic, welcomes everyone to his garden, and loves life 🍎
He hates children because they call him names 🚫
He only cares about making money 💰
answer: He is highly optimistic, welcomes everyone to his garden, and loves life 🍎
explanation: Brilliant! Unlike Derry, who hides away due to his burnt face, Mr. Lamb has a tin leg but embraces life fully. He keeps his gates open, makes crab apple jelly, and focuses on the beauty of the world! ☀️
hint: He keeps his garden gates wide open for anyone to enter.

question: How does Derry enter Mr. Lamb's garden at the beginning of the play? 🧱
options: He knocks on the front door 🚪
He walks in through the open gate 🚶
He climbs over the garden wall 🧗
He crawls under a broken fence 🕳️
answer: He climbs over the garden wall 🧗
explanation: Spot on! Even though the gate is wide open, Derry climbs over the wall because he thinks the place is empty and wants to hide away from the world. 🌿
hint: He uses physical effort to get over a barrier.

question: What is the primary reason for Derry's deep sense of alienation from society? 👤
options: He is very poor and has no friends 💸
Half of his face is heavily burnt by acid 🔥
He is a foreigner in the town 🌍
He stutters when he speaks 🗣️
answer: Half of his face is heavily burnt by acid 🔥
explanation: Perfect! Derry suffers from severe alienation and low self-esteem because acid burnt half of his face, making him hyper-aware of people's stares and cruel whispers. 😔
hint: It involves a severe physical injury to his appearance.

question: How did Mr. Lamb lose his real leg? 💥
options: In a car accident 🚗
It was bitten off by a wild animal 🐅
It was blown off in a war years ago 💣
Due to a severe medical illness 🏥
answer: It was blown off in a war years ago 💣
explanation: Great job! Mr. Lamb reveals that his leg was blown off by a bomb in a war, which is why he now has an artificial tin leg. 🦿
hint: It happened during a violent historical conflict.

question: What nickname do the local street children use to mock Mr. Lamb? 🐑
options: Tin-Man Lamb 🤖
Lamey-Lamb 🚶
Crazy Old Lamb 👴
One-Legged Lamb 🦵
answer: Lamey-Lamb 🚶
explanation: Awesome! The kids call him 'Lamey-Lamb', but he doesn't let it bother him. He accepts it with a positive perspective, knowing it fits his reality! 🛡️
hint: It rhymes and refers to his walking disability.

question: What does Mr. Lamb point out about the 'weeds' and the 'flowers' in his garden? 🌼
options: Weeds are ugly and must be destroyed ✂️
Both are growing, living plants, and the difference is just a matter of perspective 🌱
Flowers are completely useless 🥀
Weeds are poisonous to his apples ☠️
answer: Both are growing, living plants, and the difference is just a matter of perspective 🌱
explanation: Fantastic! Mr. Lamb uses the metaphor of weeds and flowers to teach Derry about perspective. Both are life, and calling one a 'weed' and the other a 'flower' is just human bias! 🍃
hint: He emphasizes that both share the same fundamental quality of life.

question: When Mr. Lamb mentions the fairy tale 'Beauty and the Beast', what is Derry's pessimistic reaction? 👹
options: He loves the story and feels hopeful 📖
He says he will never change and will stay a 'monstrous beast' forever 🐉
He thinks he is the Beauty in the story 👸
He says he has never heard of it 🤷
answer: He says he will never change and will stay a 'monstrous beast' forever 🐉
explanation: Spot on! Derry's pessimism makes him reject the story's optimistic moral. He firmly believes that unlike the Beast, he will never turn into a handsome prince. 😔
hint: He focuses on his permanent physical reality rather than a magical transformation.

question: What cruel remark did Derry overhear a woman make about his face at the bus stop? 🗣️
options: He looks like a criminal 🚨
That's a face only a mother could love 👩‍👦
He is the ugliest boy in the world 🌍
He should be kept in a hospital 🏥
answer: That's a face only a mother could love 👩‍👦
explanation: Brilliant! Derry was deeply traumatized when he heard a woman whisper, 'That's a face only a mother could love.' It shattered his self-esteem. 💔
hint: It involves the unconditional love of a specific family member.

question: How does Derry feel about his own mother kissing him? 👩‍👦
options: He loves it and feels comforted ❤️
He thinks she only does it out of duty and only on the good side of his face 💋
He wishes she would kiss him more often 🤗
He thinks she is trying to hurt him 😠
answer: He thinks she only does it out of duty and only on the good side of his face 💋
explanation: Perfect! Derry is so alienated that he even doubts his mother's love, believing she only kisses him because she has to, and notably, never on the burnt side of his face. 🏠
hint: He believes it is an act of obligation rather than pure affection.

question: What advice does Mr. Lamb give Derry about dealing with cruel comments from others? 🙉
options: Fight back and shout at them 🥊
Keep your ears shut and ignore the negativity 🤐
Report them to the police 🚓
Cry and run away 🏃
answer: Keep your ears shut and ignore the negativity 🤐
explanation: Great job! Mr. Lamb advises Derry to 'keep his ears shut'. He wants Derry to protect his inner peace by choosing not to let toxic words affect his mindset. 🛡️
hint: It involves a physical action to prevent hearing.

question: Mr. Lamb tells a story about a man who locked himself in a room. Why did the man do this? 🚪
options: He was hiding from the police 🚓
He was afraid of everything in the world that might kill him 😨
He wanted to write a book in peace ✍️
He hated his family 👨‍👩‍👦
answer: He was afraid of everything in the world that might kill him 😨
explanation: Awesome! The man was paralyzed by fear of accidents, diseases, and death, so he locked himself away. This serves as a cautionary tale against alienating oneself from life! 🌍
hint: He suffered from extreme paranoia about getting hurt.

question: What ironically happened to the man who locked himself in the room to stay safe? 🖼️
options: He lived to be a hundred years old 💯
A picture fell off the wall onto his head and killed him 💥
He starved to death 🍞
He became a famous philosopher 🎓
answer: A picture fell off the wall onto his head and killed him 💥
explanation: Spot on! In a stroke of situational irony, a picture fell on his head and killed him, proving that you cannot hide from life or death by isolating yourself! 🖼️
hint: A decorative object caused his demise.

question: Why does Mr. Lamb NOT have curtains on the windows of his house? 🪟
options: He cannot afford them 💸
He hates shutting things out and loves the light and the dark ☀️
The children stole them 🏃
He is allergic to fabric 🤧
answer: He hates shutting things out and loves the light and the dark ☀️
explanation: Fantastic! Curtains symbolize shutting out the world. Mr. Lamb refuses to have them because he embraces everything in life—both the light (optimism) and the dark (hardships). 🌗
hint: He wants to remain connected to the outside environment.

question: What is Mr. Lamb planning to make from the crab apples in his garden? 🍏
options: Apple pie 🥧
Apple cider 🍹
Crab apple jelly 🍯
Apple sauce 🥣
answer: Crab apple jelly 🍯
explanation: Brilliant! He uses a ladder and a stick to pull down the crab apples to make jelly, demonstrating how he stays active, productive, and joyful despite his physical limitations! 🪜
hint: It is a sweet, spreadable food.

question: How does Mr. Lamb view the sound of the bees in his garden? 🐝
options: He thinks they are buzzing annoyingly 🙉
He believes they are humming and singing a beautiful song 🎶
He is terrified of them stinging him 😨
He ignores them completely 😶
answer: He believes they are humming and singing a beautiful song 🎶
explanation: Perfect! While most people hear bees 'buzzing' (a harsh noise), Mr. Lamb's optimistic perspective allows him to hear them 'singing' (a beautiful melody). 🎵
hint: He describes their sound as musical.

question: What is the literary genre of Susan Hill's 'On the Face of It'? 🎭
options: A poem 📜
A short story 📖
A play / drama 🎬
An autobiography ✍️
answer: A play / drama 🎬
explanation: Great job! 'On the Face of It' is a play, written with stage directions, scenes, and dialogues, intended to be performed. 🎭
hint: It is written with dialogue and stage directions.

question: Derry claims that people are afraid of him. What does Mr. Lamb gently suggest Derry is actually afraid of? 🪞
options: The dark 🌑
Dogs 🐕
Himself and facing the world 🌍
The police 🚓
answer: Himself and facing the world 🌍
explanation: Awesome! Mr. Lamb realizes that Derry is projecting. It's not just that people are afraid of Derry's face; Derry is terrified of accepting himself and engaging with the world. 🧭
hint: It points to his own internal fears rather than external ones.

question: What does Derry say his family worries about regarding his future? 🔮
options: How he will pass his exams 📝
How he will ever get on in the world with that face 😔
How he will learn to drive 🚗
How he will make money 💰
answer: How he will ever get on in the world with that face 😔
explanation: Spot on! Derry overheard his parents pitying him, wondering what will happen to him in the future because of his severe facial disfigurement. This deepens his trauma. 🏚️
hint: They are concerned about his ability to survive in society due to his appearance.

question: Mr. Lamb points out that Derry has two arms, two legs, eyes, and ears. What is he trying to teach Derry? 💪
options: That he can join the army 🪖
That he has the physical capability and potential to do as well as, or better than, anyone else 🚀
That he should become an athlete 🏃
That he doesn't need to work 🛋️
answer: That he has the physical capability and potential to do as well as, or better than, anyone else 🚀
explanation: Brilliant! Mr. Lamb is trying to rebuild Derry's self-esteem. He wants Derry to focus on what he *has* rather than what he has *lost*. 🧠
hint: He is highlighting Derry's potential to succeed.

question: Some people tell Derry that people with disabilities should stay with 'their own kind'. How does Derry react to this idea? 🌐
options: He thinks it's a wonderful idea 👍
He thinks a world of just blind or deaf people would be terrible and absurd 🚫
He wants to build a special hospital 🏥
He completely ignores the idea 😶
answer: He thinks a world of just blind or deaf people would be terrible and absurd 🚫
explanation: Fantastic! Derry actually shows common sense here, realizing that segregation is absurd. He asks Mr. Lamb what kind of world it would be if everyone was grouped by their impairments! 🌍
hint: He strongly disagrees with segregating people.

question: What is the primary difference in how Derry and Mr. Lamb handle their respective physical impairments? ⚖️
options: Both hide from the world 🙈
Derry lets it destroy his self-esteem, while Mr. Lamb accepts it and embraces life fully 🌈
Mr. Lamb cries about it, while Derry is proud 😢
Both seek medical operations 🩺
answer: Derry lets it destroy his self-esteem, while Mr. Lamb accepts it and embraces life fully 🌈
explanation: Perfect! This contrast sets them up as character foils. Derry's impairment leads to pessimism and alienation, while Mr. Lamb's leads to empathy and optimism! 🌻
hint: One is pessimistic, the other is optimistic.

question: How old is Derry in the play? 👦
options: 10 years old 🎂
14 years old 🎈
18 years old 🎓
21 years old 🚗
answer: 14 years old 🎈
explanation: Great job! Derry is a 14-year-old boy. His young age makes his deep pessimism and alienation even more tragic, but also makes him open to Mr. Lamb's guidance. 🌱
hint: He is in his early teenage years.

question: What does Mr. Lamb mean when he says his life consists of 'Watching, listening, thinking'? 🧘
options: He is a spy 🕵️
He actively engages with the beauty of nature and human experiences rather than shutting them out 🌻
He watches too much television 📺
He is writing a novel ✍️
answer: He actively engages with the beauty of nature and human experiences rather than shutting them out 🌻
explanation: Awesome! Mr. Lamb finds joy in mindfulness and observation. He lives richly in his mind and heart, proving that physical limitations do not limit one's experience of life. 🧠
hint: It reflects his mindful and appreciative approach to life.

question: Why does Derry say people look at him and pretend not to notice his face? 👀
options: Because he wears a mask 🎭
Because they are polite 🎩
Because they are secretly afraid and don't want to show their discomfort 😨
Because his face is completely normal 👤
answer: Because they are secretly afraid and don't want to show their discomfort 😨
explanation: Spot on! Derry is highly perceptive. He knows people are shocked or disgusted by his burns, but they act 'polite' out of awkwardness or fear, which only alienates him more. 😔
hint: It stems from their own internal discomfort and fear.

question: What is Derry's mother's attitude towards Mr. Lamb when Derry says he wants to go back? 👩
options: She encourages him to go make a friend 🤗
She forbids him to go, saying she has heard bad things about the old man 🛑
She wants to go with him 🚶‍♀️
She offers to bake a cake for Mr. Lamb 🍰
answer: She forbids him to go, saying she has heard bad things about the old man 🛑
explanation: Brilliant! The mother represents societal prejudice. She judges Mr. Lamb based on rumors and tries to restrict Derry, showing how she unknowingly contributes to his isolation. 🚧
hint: She relies on local gossip and warns her son.

question: How does Derry demonstrate his transformation when talking to his mother? 🦋
options: He agrees to stay in his room forever 🛌
He defies her and insists on returning to the garden, showing he finally wants to engage with life 🏃
He decides to run away to another city 🚂
He yells at her and breaks things 💥
answer: He defies her and insists on returning to the garden, showing he finally wants to engage with life 🏃
explanation: Fantastic! For the first time, Derry stands up for his own freedom. Mr. Lamb's empathy has sparked a desire in him to overcome his fears and connect with the world! 🌟
hint: He rebels against her overprotective nature.

question: When Derry returns to the garden at the end of the play, what tragic event does he discover? 🪜
options: The garden has been sold 🏡
Mr. Lamb has fallen from his ladder while picking apples 💥
Mr. Lamb has moved away 🚂
The apples have all rotted 🍏
answer: Mr. Lamb has fallen from his ladder while picking apples 💥
explanation: Perfect! In a tragic climax, Derry runs back to the garden only to find that Mr. Lamb has fallen from the ladder, presumably to his death. 🥀
hint: It involves the old man and his apple-picking equipment.

question: What does Derry's weeping at the end of the play signify? 😢
options: He is crying because his face hurts 🤕
It signifies his profound grief for his friend and the awakening of his own emotional empathy 💖
He is sad that he didn't get any jelly 🍯
He is scared of his mother 👩
answer: It signifies his profound grief for his friend and the awakening of his own emotional empathy 💖
explanation: Great job! Derry's tears show that his heart, which was hardened by alienation, has melted. He finally connected with someone, making the loss devastating but transformative. 🦋
hint: It shows he has finally formed a meaningful connection.

question: What is the significance of the play's title, 'On the Face of It'? 🎭
options: It is a play about makeup 💄
It suggests that things and people may appear one way on the surface, but are very different underneath 🪞
It is about a famous painting 🖼️
It refers only to Derry's burnt face 🔥
answer: It suggests that things and people may appear one way on the surface, but are very different underneath 🪞
explanation: Awesome! The idiom 'on the face of it' means 'superficially'. The play explores how society judges people by their appearance (surface) rather than their true inner self. 🧭
hint: It implies looking beyond superficial appearances.

question: How did Derry originally feel about the word 'acid'? 🧪
options: He thought it was a cool science experiment 🔬
He said it didn't just burn his face, it 'ate him up' inside out 🔥
He wanted to study it in school 📚
He had no feelings about it 😶
answer: He said it didn't just burn his face, it 'ate him up' inside out 🔥
explanation: Spot on! Derry expresses deep trauma, stating the acid ate his face and ate his soul. It symbolizes how the physical injury destroyed his inner self-esteem. 🥀
hint: He feels the damage went far beyond just his skin.

question: Why does Mr. Lamb leave his front door open? 🚪
options: The lock is broken 🔧
He wants to welcome anyone and everyone, showing his complete trust in the world 🤗
He forgets to close it 🤷
He wants the street dogs to come in 🐕
answer: He wants to welcome anyone and everyone, showing his complete trust in the world 🤗
explanation: Brilliant! An open door is a powerful motif in the play. It represents Mr. Lamb's open heart, optimism, and his refusal to shut out the world. 🌍
hint: It is a deliberate choice to show hospitality.

question: What does Derry think Mr. Lamb is doing when Mr. Lamb changes the subject to 'crab apples'? 🍏
options: Trying to sell him apples 💰
Changing the subject because he is afraid to talk about Derry's face, just like everyone else 😒
Showing off his garden 🌳
Getting hungry 🍽️
answer: Changing the subject because he is afraid to talk about Derry's face, just like everyone else 😒
explanation: Fantastic! Because of his past trauma, Derry assumes Mr. Lamb is just another adult who is uncomfortable looking at his burns, though Mr. Lamb actually just doesn't judge him for it. ⚖️
hint: Derry projects his past negative experiences onto Mr. Lamb's actions.

question: What is the key element that helps Derry overcome his deep-rooted pessimism? 🌱
options: A magical medicine 💊
Mr. Lamb's unwavering empathy, acceptance, and positive perspective 🌻
His mother's strict rules 👩
Winning a lot of money 💵
answer: Mr. Lamb's unwavering empathy, acceptance, and positive perspective 🌻
explanation: Perfect! Mr. Lamb doesn't pity Derry. Instead, he treats him as an equal and shares a philosophy of acceptance, which slowly breaks down Derry's walls of alienation. 🕊️
hint: It is the emotional support he receives in the garden.

question: When Mr. Lamb says, 'Everything's the same, but everything is different,' what is he referring to? 🌍
options: The weather ⛅
The underlying unity of all life, despite outward physical differences 🌱
The types of apples in the garden 🍏
The houses in the neighborhood 🏘️
answer: The underlying unity of all life, despite outward physical differences 🌱
explanation: Great job! This is the core of his philosophy. Whether you are a weed, a flower, an old man with a tin leg, or a boy with a burnt face—we are all connected by the spark of life! ✨
hint: It points to a universal connection between all living things.

question: What does Derry promise Mr. Lamb before he runs back home? 🏃
options: That he will never return 🚫
That he will bring his mother 👩
That he will come back to the garden to help him 🤝
That he will buy the house 🏡
answer: That he will come back to the garden to help him 🤝
explanation: Awesome! Derry promises he will return to help pick the apples. This promise is crucial because it marks his commitment to stepping out of his isolation. 🌟
hint: He commits to returning to the garden.

question: Why is Derry surprised when Mr. Lamb says he has 'hundreds of friends'? 👥
options: Because Mr. Lamb lives alone in a big empty house 🏠
Because Mr. Lamb is very rude 😠
Because Mr. Lamb is poor 💸
Because Mr. Lamb is famous 🌟
answer: Because Mr. Lamb lives alone in a big empty house 🏠
explanation: Spot on! Derry, viewing the world through a literal lens, cannot understand how a man living alone can have 'friends' everywhere. Mr. Lamb views anyone he meets as a potential friend. 🌻
hint: It contrasts Mr. Lamb's living situation with his social outlook.

question: What does Derry tell his mother about what he wants to do in the garden? 🌳
options: He wants to steal apples 🍏
He wants to sit, look, listen, and think, just like Mr. Lamb 🧘
He wants to chop down the trees 🪓
He wants to sleep there all day 🛌
answer: He wants to sit, look, listen, and think, just like Mr. Lamb 🧘
explanation: Brilliant! Derry has internalized Mr. Lamb's positive philosophy. He tells his mother he wants to engage with the world—listening and thinking—rather than hiding in his room. 🧠
hint: He wants to adopt Mr. Lamb's mindful approach to life.

question: What does the tin leg symbolize in the context of the play? 🦿
options: Mr. Lamb's wealth 💰
A physical impairment that does not restrict a person's inner spirit or joy for life 🌟
A punishment for his past crimes ⛓️
A new medical invention 🏥
answer: A physical impairment that does not restrict a person's inner spirit or joy for life 🌟
explanation: Fantastic! While Derry's burnt face crippled his soul, Mr. Lamb's tin leg did not break his spirit. It symbolizes resilience and the power of a positive mindset! 🛡️
hint: It represents an injury that couldn't hold him back.

question: When Derry says he is a 'devil', what psychological state is he exhibiting? 😈
options: Extreme arrogance 😎
Profound self-hatred and internalized societal prejudice 💔
A playful sense of humor 😂
A desire to act in movies 🎬
answer: Profound self-hatred and internalized societal prejudice 💔
explanation: Perfect! Society has treated Derry like a monster for so long that he has internalized this prejudice, viewing himself as a 'devil' and displaying zero self-esteem. 🏚️
hint: It shows he has adopted society's negative view of himself.

question: What excuse does Derry's mother use to justify why she doesn't want him going back to the old man's house? 👩
options: She needs him to clean the house 🧹
She says she has been warned by people and heard bad things about him 🗣️
She says the garden is too far away 🗺️
She says it is going to rain 🌧️
answer: She says she has been warned by people and heard bad things about him 🗣️
explanation: Great job! The mother acts out of prejudice and fear of the unknown. She relies on local gossip rather than allowing Derry to form his own experiences. 🚧
hint: She relies on rumors and gossip.

question: How does Derry describe his own face when he looks in the mirror? 🪞
options: He says he is handsome 😎
He says he is afraid of himself 😨
He says he looks like his father 👨
He says he doesn't care 🤷
answer: He says he is afraid of himself 😨
explanation: Awesome! This highlights his deep trauma. He tells Mr. Lamb, 'When I look in the mirror and see it, I'm afraid of me,' showing that his worst enemy is his own self-perception. 😔
hint: It reflects his severe lack of self-esteem.

question: Mr. Lamb says, 'People are never just nothing.' What does he mean by this? 🌍
options: People are always causing trouble 😠
Every human being has inherent value and significance, regardless of appearance 💎
People are physically heavy ⚖️
Nobody exists 🫥
answer: Every human being has inherent value and significance, regardless of appearance 💎
explanation: Spot on! Mr. Lamb refuses to write anyone off as worthless. He teaches Derry that every person has value, breaking down Derry's cynical view of humanity. 🌻
hint: It affirms the intrinsic worth of every individual.

question: What is the primary literary function of Mr. Lamb in the play? 🎭
options: He is the villain 🦹
He serves as a catalyst for Derry's emotional and psychological awakening 🌱
He is a comedic relief character 😂
He is just a background extra 🌳
answer: He serves as a catalyst for Derry's emotional and psychological awakening 🌱
explanation: Brilliant! Mr. Lamb's empathetic and optimistic nature challenges Derry's worldview, ultimately inspiring him to change his attitude towards life! 🦋
hint: He initiates a major change in the protagonist.

question: What physical barrier does Derry cross at the beginning of the play, which symbolically represents him breaking into a new world? 🧱
options: A locked door 🚪
A glass window 🪟
The garden wall 🧗
A deep river 🌊
answer: The garden wall 🧗
explanation: Fantastic! Climbing the wall is both a physical and symbolic act. It represents his transition from his isolated, fearful life into Mr. Lamb's open, optimistic world! ✨
hint: It is a brick structure around the garden.

question: Why does Derry get angry when people try to comfort him by saying 'there are people worse off than you'? 😠
options: He thinks they are lying 🤥
He feels it doesn't change the reality of his burnt face or his personal suffering 🥀
He wants to be the worst off 🥇
He doesn't understand what they mean 🤷
answer: He feels it doesn't change the reality of his burnt face or his personal suffering 🥀
explanation: Perfect! Derry realizes that knowing blind or deaf people exist doesn't magically fix his face or stop people from staring at him. Platitudes don't heal his trauma. 😔
hint: It dismisses his valid personal pain.

question: At the climax of the play, what does Derry scream out as he stands in the garden? 🗣️
options: 'I hate this place!' 😠
'I came back! You see, I came back!' 🏃
'Help me!' 🆘
'Where are the apples?' 🍏
answer: 'I came back! You see, I came back!' 🏃
explanation: Great job! This is a moment of immense triumph for Derry. Despite his mother's orders and his own fears, he kept his promise and returned, proving his newfound courage! 🌟
hint: He proudly announces his return.

question: What creates the profound sense of tragedy at the very end of the play? 🥀
options: Derry runs away again 🏃
Mr. Lamb dies just as Derry finally learns to connect and embrace life 💔
The garden catches fire 🔥
Derry's mother locks him up 🚪
answer: Mr. Lamb dies just as Derry finally learns to connect and embrace life 💔
explanation: Awesome! The tragedy lies in the timing. Just as Derry breaks free from his psychological prison to embrace his new friend, that friend is taken away from him. 🦋
hint: It involves the sudden loss of his mentor.

question: What does the word 'empathy' mean in the context of Mr. Lamb's behavior? 🤝
options: Feeling sorry for someone and giving them money 💸
The ability to deeply understand and share the feelings of another person 🌻
Ignoring someone's problems 🙈
Making fun of someone 😂
answer: The ability to deeply understand and share the feelings of another person 🌻
explanation: Spot on! Mr. Lamb doesn't pity Derry; he empathizes with him. Because he also has an impairment, he understands Derry's pain but guides him toward healing. 💖
hint: It involves a deep, shared emotional understanding.

question: What is the ultimate message Susan Hill conveys about physical disabilities? 🌟
options: They ruin a person's life completely 🛑
It is societal prejudice and one's own mindset that cause the most harm, not the physical impairment itself 🧠
They should be hidden away 🙈
Only medicine can fix them 💊
answer: It is societal prejudice and one's own mindset that cause the most harm, not the physical impairment itself 🧠
explanation: Brilliant! The play beautifully demonstrates that Derry's true handicap is his fear and society's cruelty, while Mr. Lamb proves that a positive mindset can conquer physical limitations! 🌈
hint: It points to internal attitudes and social judgment as the real barriers.

question: Why does Derry finally tell his mother, 'I want to go there... and listen to things. Listen and look'? 🦋
options: Because he is bored of his room 🛌
Because Mr. Lamb has awakened a desire in him to truly engage with the world and break his alienation 🌱
Because he wants to spy on the neighbors 🕵️
Because he is hungry for apples 🍏
answer: Because Mr. Lamb has awakened a desire in him to truly engage with the world and break his alienation 🌱
explanation: Perfect! This line shows Derry's complete transformation. He no longer wants to hide; he wants to look, listen, and participate in the beauty of life! ✨
hint: It shows his new readiness to experience life.
